## ValueTypeConstructors.reference() method

A reference to one object of `resource`<!-- -->, in either form: an [IdentityReference](./contracts.identityreference.md) or a [SelectorReference](./contracts.selectorreference.md)<!-- -->.

**Signature:**

```typescript
reference<T = unknown, Id = unknown, R extends string = string>(scope: () => ReferenceScope, resource: R, cardinality: 'one', options?: ValueTypeOptions): ValueType<ObjectReferenceVariant<T, Id, R>>;
```

## Exceptions

`TypeError` when `scope` is not a function, `resource` is not a non-empty string, or `cardinality` is neither `'one'` nor `'many'`<!-- -->; and, when the value type is used, when `scope` returns something other than an app and its resource table.

## Remarks

`scope` returns the app the references belong to and its resource table: the app contract itself (a [ReferenceScope](./contracts.referencescope.md)<!-- -->). The table supplies the identifier value type of `resource` and of every resource a container can name. It is a thunk so that record types of mutually referencing resources can compose: constructing the value type never calls it, while encoding, decoding, and schema use do.

On the wire a reference is `{"reference": {…}}` (see [ReferenceWire](./contracts.referencewire.md)<!-- -->). Encoding reads only the data fields and never calls `resolve`<!-- -->, so a bound reference and a plain [ObjectReferenceData](./contracts.objectreferencedata.md) descriptor encode alike. Every level of the reference (its containers and entries too) must name the scope's `app`<!-- -->; a missing or different `app` is an issue at that level's `app`<!-- -->, and `app` is never written to the wire. Decoding sets the scope's `app` at every level and hands the decoded [ReferenceData](./contracts.referencedata.md) to `DecodeContext.bindReference`<!-- -->. A materialized [ReferenceList](./contracts.referencelist.md) is `t.array(t.reference(scope, resource, 'one'))`<!-- -->.

Every resolvable object needs its resolving operation in the scope's table: the reference and every container need `get`<!-- -->. The wire schema admits only such resources, so encoding, decoding, the runtime's check of raw requests, and the derived JSON Schema all apply the rule; a position whose resource has no `get` admits nothing.

The SDK type is the bound reference, which is what decoding produces. An input position can be typed by the data form instead ([ObjectReferenceData](./contracts.objectreferencedata.md)<!-- -->): the value type is assignable to a value type of the data form, because every bound reference is valid data.
